sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa-New Zealand Double Taxation Agreement (2011, in force)
Samoa-Australia Double Taxation Agreement (2009, in force)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus)

No dedicated standalone bilateral investment treaty with the United States, China, or Hong Kong is currently in force for Samoa; foreign investment is governed by Samoa's Foreign Investment Act and reviewed by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended, including the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018 and International Companies (Amendment) Act 2019) mandating maintenance of a beneficial ownership register; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2021 (consolidating and replacing the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and the Prevention of Terrorism Financing Act 2012); SIFA AML/CFT Compliance Guidelines for International Companies; Financial Intelligence Unit directives issued under the AML/CFT regime.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) via Licensed Registered Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Samoa (Convention in force for Samoa since 1 March 2019); consular legalization only for destination states outside the Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (English statutory original, with optional Chinese supplementary translation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SIFA-stamped copy filed through the Licensed Registered Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency including Register of Directors, Shareholders and Secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration and Beneficial Ownership Register Extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Registered Agent (SIFA-approved, holding the beneficial ownership register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Agent Consent Certificate and Registered Office Confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Tax Exemption Certificate or Offshore Tax Status Confirmation Letter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) with Ministry of Revenue coordination
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Samoa

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence, including identity verification of all beneficial owners holding 25% or more (or effective control); mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and applicants against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list, Samoa domestic designated persons list maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and the Financial Intelligence Unit of Samoa; foreign and domestic PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification; non-verifiable or politically exposed beneficial owners cause automatic escalation and possible rejection of the nomination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) eServices online registry; name search and reservation must be filed exclusively through a SIFA-licensed Registered Agent holding an approved electronic filing credential
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory registered name must be in English or Latin script; no Samoan-language requirement applies to International Companies. Foreign-language trading names (including Chinese business names) may be adopted only as secondary informal designations; the Memorandum and Articles and all statutory returns must be in English. A full Chinese-language version of the charter may be maintained solely as an unofficial supplementary convenience copy and must not displace the English legally operative text.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the Licensed Registered Agent may reserve one or more alternative names; a written administrative appeal of the negative name determination must be lodged with the Registrar of International Companies at SIFA within 14 calendar days of the notice of refusal; if SIFA confirms the refusal, further administrative review may be pursued before the Minister responsible for financial services within 30 days, and final judicial review lies with the Supreme Court of Samoa under the International Companies Act 1987 and applicable judicial review procedures.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual operations are fully permissible for the ISIC 4791 B2B cross-border marketplace business; however, every Samoa International Company must maintain a physical statutory registered office in Samoa at the office of its Licensed Registered Agent, and the company itself is not required to lease or staff any additional physical premises in Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - quantified probability below 10% per annum for a standard low-risk International Company; SIFA and the AML/CFT supervisory authority retain statutory inspection powers and may conduct unannounced physical on-site inspections of the registered office and beneficial ownership records where a risk event triggers regulatory review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation fee for International Company including initial name clearance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the International Companies Act 1987 and SIFA fee regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Formal name search and name reservation administrative fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SIFA collected through Licensed Registered Agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed Registered Agent annual retainer incl. statutory registered office and custodian of statutory records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 300-600 per annum for standard International Companies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office maintenance component of agent retainer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark component bundled within the annual agent retainer

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of corporate documents and UBO declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per-document notary tariff in Apia

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille legalization bundle for up to seven corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade of Samoa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official MFAT apostille fee schedule; consular legalization alternative applies for non-Hague destination states

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding, PEP and sanctions screening for beneficial owners (up to three natural persons)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for standard low-risk CDD/EDD under AML/CFT Act 2021

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, drafting of Memorandum and Articles, and reserved name advisory
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for an offshore International Company incorporation package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 6–15 (incorporation), ss. 16–18 (memorandum and articles), s. 87 (registered office and agent), and ss. 61–74 (directors, secretary, and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (Form 1) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; one ordinary share may be issued at par. No escrow account or capital deposit is required. Share capital may be denominated in any currency approved by SIFA.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers adopt the Company's Memorandum and Articles of Association and subscribe for one ordinary share each, fully paid. The registered office of the Company is fixed at the licensed service provider's address in Apia, Samoa, and the registered agent under the International Companies Act 1987 is appointed. The following persons are appointed first directors, each to hold office until the first annual general meeting or until successors are appointed. The following persons are appointed Corporate Secretary and Chief Executive Officer, with the powers and duties contained in the Company's governance rules. The directors are authorized to execute all documents and pay all registration fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Due Diligence Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through a licensed SIFA service provider. The proposed name must end with 'Limited' and must not be identical or deceptively similar to any name already registered. Provide identification and background documents of subscribers for anti-money-laundering due diligence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation of corporate subscriber (if any)
Passport copy of each individual subscriber/director
Bank or professional reference letter for each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or reserved subject to conditions, file a revised name application within 10 business days; no filing fee refund applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitution Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed International Company Service Provider / Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association. Each subscriber must sign the share subscription page, and signatures must be witnessed and notarized. Obtain consents to act from each proposed director and the corporate secretary.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA queries any constitutional provision, amend the relevant article by resolution of subscribers and re-notarize before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) with the executed constitution documents through the licensed service provider. Pay the official filing fee by SWIFT wire transfer and retain the receipt as proof of submission.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, cure the deficiency in writing within 14 days by supplying the requested particulars or corrections; the application may be withdrawn and the fee partially refunded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and date of incorporation. The company comes into legal existence on that date. Ensure the registered agent and registered office details are recorded in the SIFA register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Errors in the Certificate or register are corrected by written application to the Registrar under s. 12 within 21 days of issuance; supporting evidence of the correct particulars must accompany the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Post-Incorporation Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to pass the first board resolution covering share subscription allotment, adoption of the registered office, and appointment of officers. File the notice of directors and officers with SIFA and maintain the statutory registers at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing within 30 days attracts a late fee; after that, an application for late filing relief with a letter of explanation may be submitted to SIFA for remission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — licensing would only apply if a physical wholesale or warehousing presence is later established; pure electronic B2B marketplace operations are exempt
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — International Companies are exempt from the Domestic Business Licence in Samoa; no operating permit is required for cross-border electronic B2B wholesale platform activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical manufacturing, land-disturbance, or discharge-producing activity; the company maintains only a virtual platform with an administrative office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; if the administrative office generates general solid waste, the company must comply with the Waste Management Act 2010 and PUMA municipal waste collection standards. If any future physical warehouse is established, a Pollution Discharge Permit under the Water Resources Management Act 2008 would be required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) for the administrative office; occupational registration with the Department of Labour under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 covering workplace safety and employee records; building occupancy permit for any leased office premises confirming structural and electrical safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue (MOR), Samoa - central tax administration headed by the Commissioner of Revenue; official eServices portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws (business TIN registration, VAGST returns, payroll returns, tax clearance certificates). Customs export formalities are processed by Samoa Customs Service through the ASYCUDA World national clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 through a licensed registered agent at the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour); Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing issue in 3-5 working days with no minimum capital requirement. Step 2 - The IC is not required to obtain a revenue TIN for its exempt offshore business; it maintains tax-exempt status through annual Registrar renewal and compliance with the non-resident business restriction. Step 3 - Obtain a 9-digit MOR Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) at the first point of contact with the Samoan tax system, namely voluntary VAGST registration, employer PAYE/WHT registration, customs import transactions, or any taxable activity in Samoa; the licensed agent lodges Form TIN-01 with certified incorporation documents, director and beneficial ownership declarations (AML/CFT Act 2018), and the registered office/agent certificate; TIN issuance takes 5-10 business days. Step 4 - Quote the TIN on all tax returns, customs declarations and Revenue correspondence; a VAGST registration number is the same TIN with a 'VG' suffix.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - under sections 198-202 of the International Companies Act 1987, the IC enjoys a statutory territorial exemption from all Samoan taxes, including income tax, withholding tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, gift and estate duties, and is free from exchange control. The exemption applies only where the IC does not carry on business with Samoa residents, has no Samoan-source income, and has no permanent establishment in Samoa as recharacterized under the Income Tax Act 2019 general anti-avoidance rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box entity classification election. Available statutory elections relevant to an IC: (1) voluntary VAGST registration under section 10 of the VAGST Act 2003 to recover Samoan input tax on local overheads; (2) employer registration election for PAYE/withholding tax once Samoan employees are hired; (3) re-domiciliation or migration election converting the IC into an ordinary company under the Companies Act 2006, which surrenders the section 198 exemption; and (4) elections are not available for consolidated or exempt filing with MOR - an IC files annual returns solely with the Registrar of International and Foreign Companies. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are neutralized by the Income Tax Act 2019 general anti-avoidance and substance-over-form provisions; no elective hybrid mismatch or consolidated tax regime exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) - Samoa's destination-principle value added tax levied under the VAGST Act 2003 as amended and administered under the Tax Administration Act 2019.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 100,000 (Samoan Tala, approx. USD 37,000) of annual taxable supplies; registration is mandatory once actual or reasonably expected turnover meets or exceeds SAT 100,000, with voluntary registration available for exporters and suppliers of zero-rated goods and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, API, or government pre-approval e-invoicing mandate exists in Samoa. Suppliers must issue invoices containing prescribed particulars (supplier and recipient identity, VAGST registration number, nature of supply, tax-exclusive and inclusive amounts, and VAGST amount). VAGST returns and customs declarations are lodged electronically through the MOR eServices portal and the ASYCUDA World customs clearance system, which interoperate for import and export control, but individual invoices are not cleared or stamped in real time.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (a) goods physically exported from Samoa under a valid customs export declaration and (b) services supplied to a non-resident where the benefit of the service is received wholly outside Samoa and is not consumed or enjoyed in Samoa, including B2B marketplace platform and cross-border digital wholesale services. An International Company whose marketplace revenue is derived exclusively from offshore counterparties is outside the scope of VAGST entirely (no output tax liability); if the IC voluntarily registers, the same offshore services qualify for zero-rating. Substantiation requires an export contract, commercial invoice, customs export declaration (goods), transport documents, bank credit evidence, and, for digital services, non-resident evidence and platform usage logs proving offshore consumption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World) - mandatory exit record evidencing physical removal of goods from Samoa
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / electronic waybill - through-transport document evidencing export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice - evidencing receipt of the foreign sales consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner of Revenue may deny, claw back, and assess any zero-rated refund or exemption where export documentation is false, incomplete, or non-genuine (VAGST Act 2003 ss. 53-62 and Tax Administration Act 2019). Civil exposure includes repayment of the refunded tax, shortfall penalties of 20% for failure to take reasonable care and up to 100% for intentional or evasive false statements, plus statutory late-payment interest of approximately 2% per month or part thereof. Criminal exposure includes fines and imprisonment for fraudulent export declarations and tax evasion under the Customs Act 1977 and Tax Administration Act 2019. For International Companies, misuse of the section 198 exemption to channel Samoan-source activity triggers immediate de-exemption with full income tax assessment from inception, and the licensed registered agent may be jointly penalized for facilitating the non-compliant structure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), acting under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, the Exchange Control Act 1976, and the Exchange Control Regulations 1979, as the sole monetary authority and exchange control administrator for the Independent State of Samoa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa maintains a regulated but effectively convertible exchange control regime for current account transactions. Current account payments, including trade settlement, service fees, dividends, and management fees, may be processed through an authorized dealer in Samoa upon presentation of authentic underlying commercial documentation. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity subscription, shareholder loans, M&A proceeds, and capital repatriation, require either CBS approval or an exemption certificate where available. An International Company (IC) organized under the Samoa International Companies Act 1987 is treated as non-resident for exchange control purposes and is permitted to maintain fully foreign-currency-denominated accounts without mandatory conversion into Samoan Talā (WST). Profit remittance by an IC is subject to minimal friction provided the IC does not carry on business with Samoa residents, does not hold Samoan land or trust assets requiring licensing, and maintains transparent beneficial ownership records. The principal practical hurdles are anti-money laundering and know-your-customer compliance rather than exchange control exhaustion; unsubstantiated cross-border settlements or transactions with prohibited jurisdictions will be rejected by the correspondent banking layer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident commercial enterprises in Samoa, CBS Exchange Control Regulations require export proceeds to be repatriated to Samoa through an authorized dealer within 90 days from the date of shipment, with mandatory conversion into WST where the exporter trades locally in WST. A resident exporter must retain documentary evidence of the export contract, customs export declaration, and payment receipt for audit by CBS upon demand. For a non-resident Samoa International Company engaged in cross-border B2B marketplace facilitation, no export-proceeds surrender is mandated: the IC must be listed as the exporter or principal on the relevant commercial documents only when goods are sold into Samoa. In the typical offshore IC distribution model where the platform controls sales from third-country warehouses to overseas buyers, the IC's foreign-currency receipts are retained freely in the offshore USD/EUR settlement account, provided the IC maintains a written non-resident declaration with its registered agent and files an annual compliance certificate with CBS if requested.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD and WST Current Account; Capital Escrow Account not separately required for IC capital injections if supported by a board resolution and registered agent certification
Capital Escrow Account for initial shareholder capital and an Operational Foreign Currency Settlement Account for B2B platform flows

Operational Foreign Currency Current Account; Capital Escrow facility only where CBS exchange control pre-approval is secured and the IC presents a no-objection letter from the International Financial Services Unit

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for secondary settlement flows, Low for primary treasury custody. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, or Revolut Business may be used as payment aggregation rails for B2B marketplace receipts and disbursements, but they are not licensed by the Central Bank of Samoa and cannot substitute for a commercial bank relationship. Legal constraints include: (i) the IC must execute a cross-border payment processing agreement in writing with the EMI, and the EMI must maintain settlement funds in segregated accounts at a top-tier OECD bank; (ii) all funds landing in Samoa must ultimately be routed to a CBS-licensed bank for clearing; (iii) the EMI must be established in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction and must provide full transaction-level reporting to the Samoan bank upon request; and (iv) use of an EMI may trigger enhanced due diligence if the aggregate monthly throughput exceeds USD 100,000, in which case a treasury reconciliation pack, signed auditor confirmation, and up-to-date sanctions screening must be maintained.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: As a general CBS-regulated practice, every non-resident International Company opening a bank account in Samoa must have at least one director or an appointed authorised signatory physically attend the bank's onboarding interview at a Samoan branch for signature verification and intended-activity explanation. Remote opening may be approved solely on a case-by-case basis where: (a) the signatory's identity document is notarised or apostilled, (b) the notarisation is countersigned by a Samoan notary public or the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalisation unit, (c) the video interview is conducted by the bank's compliance manager in real time, and (d) the registered agent produces a board resolution confirming the signatory's authority. Beneficial owners holding more than 25% of the IC must provide certified passport copies, proof of address issued within the last 3 months, and a sworn statement of source of wealth. Banks will generally reject a fully remote application where the IC has no prior relationship with the registered agent or where the ownership chain involves a jurisdiction with strategic AML deficiencies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border electronic settlements via Alibaba/Pay, Payoneer, or other platform rails without a demonstrable goods-and-services trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete order-level reconciliation bundle containing (i) the platform's settlement statement mentioning every transaction ID and invoice number; (ii) commercial invoices and packing lists for each sales order; (iii) third-party logistics shipment tracking and delivery confirmation; (iv) customs declarations or electronic export notifications; and (v) an auditor-prepared treasury report showing that the settlement amounts match the invoiced receivable ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through bearer shares, nominee shareholders, or a chain of discretionary trust holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A current Register of Members issued by the Samoa registered agent; a declaration that no bearer shares are outstanding or, if originally issued, evidence that bearer share certificates have been cancelled and placed with a licensed custodian; full CHART of beneficial ownership up to natural persons; and a certified copy of the constitutional documentation confirming that the IC is validly registered under the International Companies Act 1987.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high capital injection or shareholder loan from a third-party jurisdiction with inadequate source-of-wealth proof.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements evidencing the accumulation of funds over at least 12 months; a notarised sworn declaration of source of wealth; a copy of the board resolution approving the injection; an updated investor register entry; and, where the capital is provided through an intermediate holding vehicle, the holding vehicle's memorandum of association and audited financial statements demonstrating lawful origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to high-risk destinations or to a dense counterparty network inconsistent with the approved platform counterparty list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A board-approved Approved Counterparty List (ACL) detailing counterparty legal names, jurisdictions, and reason for payment; trade contracts or purchase orders for each counterpart; US-EU-UN sanctions screening outputs from a licensed list-checking system; and a written compliance legal opinion from a licensed AML attorney confirming that payments do not contravene Samoa's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2018.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscriptions and shareholder loan advances should be wired from the investing entity's own bank account to the IC's beneficiary foreign-currency account at a CBS-licensed Samoan commercial bank using SWIFT MT103 for single payments under USD 50,000 and MT202 COV for larger-value transfers. The SWIFT payment fields must contain: beneficiary name matching the IC certificate exactly; the IC's registered account number; remitter name and full address; and the purpose-of-payment code corresponding to 'equity injection' under the Balance of Payments classification, typically 'FA-DIRECT INVESTMENT - EQUITY' (or Samoa's BOP code 3131 if required by the receiving bank). The remittance narrative field should include the phrase 'CAPITAL INJECTION TO SAMOA IC - NON-RESIDENT ACCOUNT' plus the registered agent's reference. To prevent freezing at the beneficiary bank, the IC must pre-clear the injection by submitting board resolution, updated register of members, and a capital verification letter from the Samoa registered agent confirming the non-resident status; the bank may require source-of-funds certification for injections exceeding USD 100,000 in any 12-month period.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements of the B2B marketplace, principal clearing rails are: (a) SWIFT MT103 bank-to-bank wire transfers for supplier payments, quoting 'INV-[invoice number]' and the relevant Incoterms in the payment narrative; (b) Commercial documentary letters of credit (L/C) issued by the Samoan bank in favour of the supplier for procurement above USD 50,000, allowing trade settlement against shipping documents; and (c) local WST clearing through Samoa's automated interbank payment system for any settlement to domestic Samoan logistics or warehouse service providers. E-commerce platform settlement receipts, e.g., from Alibaba/Pay and similar aggregators, may arrive as a single consolidated batch; the treasury management system must match the batch to individual order IDs before an internal clearing instruction is released. The IC's bank will require that all payments are made exclusively to account beneficiaries identified on the board-approved ACL and that outgoing wires include standard financial crime prevention messages consistent with the Wolfsberg correspondent banking transparency principles.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts on USD/WST, EUR/USD, and USD/GBP with a CBS-licensed commercial bank, hedged against documented commercial exposure such as supplier invoices, platform settlement currencies, and receivables conversion, with a maturity not exceeding 12 months.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST/USD or USD/CNH transacted through a non-bank financial institution outside Samoa, permissible where the underlying exposure is a genuine cross-border B2B flow and the hedge is excluded from the onshore WST deliverable market to avoid regulatory conflict with CBS exchange control.

Cross-currency swaps between USD and EUR or USD and AUD for matching mismatched procurement and settlement cashflows, available only with a licensed international bank counterparty and subject to the IC's board-approved treasury policy and CBS notification where the swap creates a foreign currency liability of the IC.

Currency options (call/put) on USD/EUR or USD/WST purchased on a premium-paid basis for protection against adverse platform-currency movements, permitted when the notional amount does not exceed 150% of forecast settlement receipts for the corresponding period and when the option is fully documented in the treasury management file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of International Company (Government Annual Licence Fee Payment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation each year; the licensed registered agent files and pays within a 30-calendar-day grace period after the anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late surcharge accrues for each commenced month of arrears up to a statutory maximum of 50% of the renewal fee; 12 months of continuous non-payment permits the Registrar to strike the International Company off the register and dissolve it, with restoration available only by regulated reinstatement application

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent in Samoa; confidential register open to inspection by the Registrar of International Companies and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the anniversary of incorporation and within 30 days after any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the Samoa AML/CFT and International Companies legislative framework, exposing the company and each defaulting director to monetary fines; persistent default may be treated by the Registrar as grounds for administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Books, Financial Records and Register Audit (internal inspection)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Office in Samoa; no public filing with the Registrar is required for Tax-Exempt Zone International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous maintenance obligation; records and registers must be produced within 7 business days of lawful demand and must cover the preceding 7 financial years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or produce statutory books and financial records is a continuing contravention of the International Companies Act 2018 carrying fines and director disqualification, and may ground a strike-off application by the Registrar

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Engagement Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed corporate services provider acting as registered agent and maintaining the registered office in Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewed annually on or before the anniversary of incorporation; agent consent and appointment documentation evidenced in the statutory corporate file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a licensed Samoa registered agent or registered office is a statutory offence punishable by fines; a continuing lapse results in cancellation of the company's registration and strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, asset or shareholder thresholds trigger a mandatory audit for a Samoa International Company; the exempt-zone regime does not require any independent statutory audit. An audit is required only where the articles of association impose it, where members holding at least 10% of the voting rights validly demand one, or where the Registrar orders an examination.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The International Companies Act 2018 does not prescribe a local GAAP for International Companies; books may be kept under IFRS (IASB), UK-adopted FRS 102 or another internationally recognised accounting standard. IFRS or a substantially equivalent standard should be applied where financial statements support cross-border payment-rail onboarding, credit assessment or investor diligence.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The confidential beneficial ownership register is maintained at the Samoa registered office. Each shareholder and any intermediate holding entity must confirm the ultimate beneficial owner(s) annually within 14 days of the anniversary of incorporation and within 30 days of any share transfer, allotment or change of control. The licensed registered agent records the confirmation in the Register of Beneficial Owners; the register is not filed with the public registry but is available for lawful inspection by the Registrar of International Companies, the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and authorised law-enforcement agencies. Any share transfer must first be approved by the board and re-registered in the Register of Members before the UBO record is updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book and Register of Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 900 per annum for a licensed Samoa registered agent, registered office, corporate secretarial maintenance and custody of statutory registers; excludes nominee directorship, banking introductions and legal drafting
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 for a voluntary certified independent audit of the B2B e-marketplace financial statements under IFRS; not statutorily required for a Samoa Tax-Exempt Zone International Company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% effective for an International Company (IC) under the tax-exempt zone regime; the standard Samoa corporate income tax headline rate for taxable resident companies is 27% (Income Tax Ordinance 2015).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income tax exemption for International Companies pursuant to section 150 of the International Companies Act 2008, covering foreign-source income, capital gains, transfers by or to non-residents, and instruments executed offshore. The only recurring fiscal cost is the annual government fee (approx. WST 265, subject to ministerial order). Exemption is forfeited if the IC derives Samoa-source income or transacts with Samoa residents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR-1 Corporate Income Tax Return — Samoa Ministry of Revenue E-Tax Portal (https://www.revenue.gov.ws). Applicable only if the IC loses exemption; exempt ICs file no CIT return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end (standard Samoa fiscal year ends 30 June; deadline 30 September).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from all Samoa-source and foreign-source business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: insert 0.00 if no Samoa-source income; attach schedule of foreign-source platform revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions (business expenses, depreciation, arm's-length service fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: insert 0.00; otherwise substantiate with contemporaneous TP documentation.
Exempt IC: 0.00; taxable IC: any Samoa-source income after deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 27% plus credits and reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: no tax payable; taxable IC: self-assess and remit with the filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: WST 200 plus 5% of the tax due per month or part thereof (capped at 100% of the tax). Late payment interest: 15% per annum. Understatement penalty: 25% of the additional tax; intentional evasion attracts 200% penalty and criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (ICA-AR) — Samoa International Companies Online Registry (e-Registry), filed by the licensed resident agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name and International Company registration number (WS-IC-XXXXX).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the Certificate of Incorporation exactly; no trading name for an offshore IC.
Physical street address of the licensed resident agent; P.O. Box alone is insufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident agent name, license number, and countersignature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Agent must be licensed under the International Companies Act 2008 and confirm ongoing representation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compliance declaration: confirm no Samoa-source business, no local real property, and no security over Samoa land.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: False declaration voids the tax exemption and triggers penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual government fee remittance (WST 265 standard fee).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fee payable in Samoa Tala via the agent; receipt number recorded.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual return penalty: WST 50 per month of arrears. Three consecutive months of default triggers administrative strike-off. A struck-off IC's contracts become voidable and assets escheat to the Registrar; reinstatement costs up to WST 500 plus Court order fees.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions paid by an exempt Samoan International Company to non-resident shareholders (statutory IC exemption overrides the general 15% non-resident dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Ordinance 2015). Profit repatriation may be executed by board resolution without Samoan WHT or exchange control approval.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not required for exempt IC distributions because no Samoa withholding tax arises. Should a treaty-claiming shareholder be denied the exemption, the protocol is: (1) file a written application with the Samoan Ministry of Revenue for a Certificate of Residence (COR) / Tax Residency Certificate (TRC); (2) attach the board resolution, audited financial statements, and proof of substance; (3) the Ministry issues the TRC within 14 business days (fee approx. WST 50); (4) the non-resident payer presents the TRC, a Form WHT-Relief self-certification, and the applicable DTA article to the Samoa Revenue to obtain a withholding tax exemption or reduced rate ruling. Samoa's active DTA network is limited (e.g., New Zealand, Vanuatu) but complemented by extensive TIEAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoa withholding tax on cross-border payments to non-residents: 15% on interest and 15% on royalties (Income Tax Ordinance 2015). For an exempt International Company, outbound royalty and interest payments attributable to foreign business are subject to 0% WHT. Where treaty relief applies, rates may be reduced to 0%–10% on submission of a valid Samoan TRC.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa has no published Local File/Master File thresholds; the arm's-length principle applies where a non-exempt IC has related-party cross-border transactions. For the tax-exempt B2B platform entity, the Samoa Revenue may require contemporaneous documentation where related-party platform fees or intercompany payments exceed WST 250,000 per annum. Prudent practice: prepare a thin Local File for annual intercompany service flows above WST 500,000, even though the IC is exempt.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not apply OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) to International Companies. However, the International Companies Act 2008 mandates a licensed resident agent, a registered physical office, and maintenance of proper accounting records. The IC exemption is conditional: no Samoa-source income, no transactions with Samoa residents, and management activities consistent with bona fide international business. Non-compliant entities are deemed shell vehicles, subject to strike-off and domestic taxation at 27%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a B2B marketplace that generates Samoa-source income (e.g., sales to Samoa residents, local fulfilment services, or accepting Samoan bank settlement) while declaring total exemption and concealing revenue from the Ministry of Revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessed tax at 27% on the undeclared worldwide income; penalty equal to 200% of the tax evaded (or WST 100,000, whichever is greater); interest at 15% per annum; criminal fine of up to WST 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years under the Income Tax Ordinance 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax where they knew or ought reasonably to have known of the concealment. Courts may order civil restitution of misappropriated funds, issue travel bans preventing departure from Samoa, and impose disqualification orders of up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an IC with no registered agent, no physical office, no accounting records, and no demonstrable commercial activity while the platform revenue flows to undisclosed beneficial owners in high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off from the International Companies Register under section 199 of the International Companies Act 2008; declaration of the IC as a dissolved and escheated company; fines on the agent up to WST 50,000; registration in the International Tax Bulletin as a 'non-compliant/transparent' entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the corporate veil under the Companies Act 2006 fraudulent trading provisions, holding directors personally accountable for the company's debts up to WST 500,000; a personal asset freeze and confiscation order may extend to beneficiaries who received hidden distributions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to implement a risk-based AML programme, failing to identify beneficial owners of the B2B marketplace's merchant accounts, or processing payments (Alibaba Pay / SWIFT wire) without enhanced due diligence where counterparties indicate sanctions exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to WST 2,000,000 against the IC and WST 500,000 against each officer under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2017; license revocation of the resident agent; suspension of the IC's right to accept wire payments; inclusion on the Samoa AML watchlist.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face personal fines of WST 250,000 and imprisonment up to 14 years for wilful blindness to money laundering. Travel bans are mandatory for accused persons; the court may order disgorgement of all platform fees earned during the breach period and prohibit re-entry to Samoa for up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Declaration / Fraud on the Registrar
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly submitting a false annual return declaration (Box D) affirming absence of Samoa-source business, or falsifying evidence of the resident agent's supervision of the marketplace platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under the International Companies Act 2008; automatic forfeiture of the IC exemption; retroactive CIT assessment for 5 years with the 200% evasion penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and the resident agent are jointly liable to the Revenue for the recalculated tax; the court may order a recovery judgment against personal estates, impose a travel ban, and issue a 15-year corporate management disqualification. Willful fraud is an extraditable offence under Samoa's Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying royalties or interest to a related non-resident entity at an inflated rate and withholding no tax, or distributing dividends from non-exempt Samoa-source reserves disguised as IC-exempt profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional assessment at 27% on the gross payment; withholding tax of 15% imposed on the gross amount; penalty of 150% of the unpaid WHT; disallowance of the interest/royalty deduction for the payer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unpaid WHT where they authorized the payment while knowing the payer was non-exempt; the court may order restitution equivalent to the tax plus penalties, freeze director bank accounts, and impose imprisonment of up to 3 years for deliberate non-remittance.
